`malariafwd` is an R interface to a SLiM + tskit forward simulator of *Plasmodium
vivax*. You run the model from R and analyse its outputs — including **ground-truth
identity-by-descent** from the recorded tree sequence.

The code chunks below are not evaluated when the vignette is built (they need SLiM and
Python `tskit`); run them locally after checking your setup.

## Setup

The model runs the external `slim` binary (SLiM ≥ 5.2) as a subprocess. The IBD and ARG
functions also need Python with `tskit` (≥ 1.0) and `numpy`, through `reticulate`:
with no Python chosen, reticulate sets up its own environment with them the first time one of
these functions runs (this needs internet once), or set `RETICULATE_PYTHON` to a Python that has
them. Nothing below runs without SLiM; without Python only the IBD and ARG sections stop. Check
both:

```{r}
library(malariafwd)
check_setup()
```

## One simulation

`vivax_params()` gives a validated parameter set (all defaults mirror the model); override
what you need. `run_sim()` launches SLiM and returns a `vivax_run` pointing at the outputs. The
run's directory appears when the run has finished, and a directory that already holds a run is
not replaced unless you pass `overwrite = TRUE`.

```{r}
p   <- vivax_params(N_HOSTS = 300, N_MOSQ = 600, BITING_RATE = 0.09)
param_info(c("N_HOSTS", "BITING_RATE"))   # every parameter: ?vivax_params or param_info()
run <- run_sim(p, seed = 1, outdir = file.path(tempdir(), "demo"))

ev <- load_events(run)      # tidy event log (data.table)
st <- load_state(run)       # per-tick host state
summarise_run(run)            # prevalence, COI, EIR, FOI, molFOB, relapses: the second half of the run
```

## Sense-check the run

`plot_diagnostics()` is a one-call health dashboard — prevalence, incidence and force of
infection by origin (FOI vs molFOB), COI, the hypnozoite reservoir, and circulating-lineage
richness over time — so you can spot extinction, saturation, or non-stationarity at a glance.

```{r}
plot_diagnostics(run)
```

## Ground-truth IBD

`ibd_pairs()` computes genome-wide IBD from the tree sequence, keyed by pedigree id, and
`ibd_lookup()` reads a pair's value (`NA` for a genome the object does not hold). Relapses are
clonal to their origin (IBD = 1):

```{r}
cs <- classify_cases(ev)                           # each case by TRUE origin
x  <- ibd_pairs(run, ids = cs$pedigree_id)
x                                                  # genomes, pairs, and where they came from
ibd_lookup(x, cs$pedigree_id[1], cs$pedigree_id[2])
ibd_relapse_origin(ev, x)                          # IBD of each relapse vs its origin (~1)
recurrences(ev, ibd = x)                           # each recurrence vs the host's earlier episodes
new_infection_diversity(run)                        # relatedness of the transmitting population
```

`ibd_pairs()` counts all shared ancestry, however far back it goes. Ask for `segments` to get
the shared blocks themselves: each a maximal stretch inherited from one common ancestor, cut at
the chromosome junctions, and tagged with that ancestor:

```{r}
sg <- ibd_pairs(run, ids = cs$pedigree_id, segments = TRUE)
head(sg$segments)    # a, b, chrom, start, end, gstart, gend, length, mrca_id, mrca_time, depth
## IBD from ancestors of the last six months only
sg$segments[depth <= 180, .(ibd_180 = sum(length) / sg$sequence_length), by = .(a, b)]
```

`mrca_time` is a tskit node time -- ticks before the **end of the run**, not an age. A "recent
ancestry only" variant filters on `depth`, the age of each segment's common ancestor measured
from the pair itself (for example `sg$segments[depth <= 180]`), never on `mrca_time` alone: that
scores a pair by when its lineage last branched rather than by how related the two genomes are,
which inverts the relapse-vs-reinfection comparison. See `?ibd_pairs`.

## Parallel sweeps

`run_grid()` runs every (parameter set × seed) in parallel via the `future` backend. Set
`workers` to the cores you can spare for a quick local multisession; for a cluster, set
`future::plan()` yourself and leave `workers = NULL`. Every set, and every cell's directory, is
checked before any cell starts. A cell that already holds its run is not run again, so calling
`run_grid()` again with the same arguments resumes a grid that stopped part-way, and adding seeds
runs only the new cells. `grid.tsv` in the grid's directory records every cell, and
`load_grid()` reads it back.

```{r}
sets <- list(
  low  = vivax_params(BITING_RATE = 0.06),
  high = vivax_params(BITING_RATE = 0.12)
)
base <- file.path(tempdir(), "sweep")
res  <- run_grid(sets, seeds = 1:10, outdir_base = base, workers = 2)
res   # one row per cell: set, seed, outdir, ok, skipped, error, extinct_tick, never_started,
      # elapsed_s, finished, slim_version, malariafwd_version, and BITING_RATE, which varies
load_grid(base)   # the same table, from grid.tsv
```

## Plots

```{r}
plot_host_state_prevalence(host_state_prevalence(st))
plot_relapse_km(time_to_relapse(run))
```

See `?run_sim`, `?ibd_pairs`, and the `DECISIONS.md` design log for more.
